title: There is no pontifical neuron, and control is distributed

statements.text: Doing several things at once, and dissociations such as fugues, sit badly with a unified controller. From what is known of the brain it is highly implausible that a pontifical neuron or neuron group acts as the control center, and a strictly hierarchical model of control may be as wrong for the brain as an intelligent creator was for nature.

sources.quote: it seems highly implausible that there is a pontifical neuron, or a pontifical-neuron group which acts as the control centre
control is distributed, not deposited despotically in self-consciousness
